message.reasoning:
We need to generate a test class for JsonSchema.getRefSchemaNode(String). Should create tests covering behavior: handling of schema root id, decoding, pointer navigation, missing node handling.

We need to set up JsonSchema instance. It has private constructor; but there is static method from(...). The class has static method JsonSchema.from(ValidationContext, SchemaLocation, JsonNodePath, JsonNode schemaNode, JsonSchema parent, boolean suppressSubSchemaRetrieval). That's probably used to create instance.

We can mock dependencies: ValidationContext, SchemaLocation, JsonNodePath, JsonNode (schemaNode). Use Mockito to stub methods used: findSchemaResourceRoot(), getSchemaNode(), getId(), etc. However findSchemaResourceRoot() is a public method of JsonSchema that probably returns itself or root; we can mock JsonSchema subclass? Can't mock final class? JsonSchema is not final, we can spy.

Simplify: create a real JsonSchema using from with minimal dependencies: ValidationContext can be constructed with real JsonMetaSchema, JsonSchemaFactory, config. Need actual classes; but they may be heavy. Instead we can use Mockito to mock JsonSchema and stub findSchemaResourceRoot() to return a mocked root schema with appropriate behavior.

But getRefSchemaNode is an instance method; it uses findSchemaResourceRoot() to get schema, then schema.getSchemaNode() to get node (JsonNode). So we can create a spy of JsonSchema where findSchemaResourceRoot() returns a mocked root schema. However JsonSchema's private fields may be needed; we can create a subclass test double.

Simpler: use Mockito to mock JsonSchema (the class under test) but we need to call real method getRefSchemaNode, not stub. Use spy on a JsonSchema instance constructed via a dummy constructor (maybe using reflection to call private constructor). Or we can create a subclass that extends JsonSchema and expose a constructor that calls super with dummy parameters. But super constructor is private, can't call. However there is a protected copy constructor; we could create a minimal JsonSchema instance via static from method, using minimal real dependencies. That may be easier.

We need to supply a ValidationContext: we can create a real JsonMetaSchema using JsonMetaSchema.getV7() maybe; but not sure. Could use JsonMetaSchema.getV7() static method. JsonSchemaFactory can be new JsonSchemaFactory.Builder().build(); Config default.

Thus:

ValidationContext vc = new ValidationContext(JsonMetaSchema.getV7(), new JsonSchemaFactory.Builder().build(), new SchemaValidatorsConfig());

SchemaLocation sl = new SchemaLocation(new AbsoluteIri("http://example.com/schema"), JsonNodePath...); need AbsoluteIri class. Might be heavy.

Alternative: mock ValidationContext, SchemaLocation, JsonNodePath, JsonNode. Use static from method which expects those. It will call super which may use methods of those objects. Might cause NPE if we don't stub. Might be easier to use Mockito.spy on a JsonSchema subclass that overrides findSchemaResourceRoot() to return a mocked root.

We can create a concrete subclass TestJsonSchema extends JsonSchema with a public constructor that calls super with dummy parameters via reflection? Actually JsonSchema's constructor is private, so subclass cannot call it. So can't extend.

Thus we need to use Mockito to mock JsonSchema (the class) but call real method using CALLS_REAL_METHODS. Example: JsonSchema schema = mock(JsonSchema.class, CALLS_REAL_METHODS); Then we need to stub findSchemaResourceRoot() to return a mocked root schema. Also stub getSchemaNode() on root schema to return a JsonNode representing a JSON document.

But JsonSchema.getSchemaNode() is defined in BaseJsonValidator maybe; but we can stub it on the root mock.

Thus:

JsonSchema root = mock(JsonSchema.class);
when(root.getSchemaNode()).thenReturn(rootNode);
when(root.getId()).thenReturn("http://example.com/root#");
when(root.isSchemaResourceRoot()).thenReturn(true); maybe not needed.

Now for the schema under test (the spy), we need findSchemaResourceRoot() to return root. So:

JsonSchema schemaUnderTest = mock(JsonSchema.class, CALLS_REAL_METHODS);
when(schemaUnderTest.findSchemaResourceRoot()).thenReturn(root);

Now we can call schemaUnderTest.getRefSchemaNode(ref) and verify behavior.

We need to construct rootNode as a JsonNode (Jackson). Use ObjectMapper to parse a JSON string.

Example JSON: {"a": {"b": 1}}.

Test cases:

1. ref = "#/a/b" => jsonPointer becomes "/a/b"? Actually code: jsonPointer = ref; if starts with "#/", substring 1 => "#/a/b" -> after substring(1) => "/a/b". Then if starts with "/", decode and node = node.at(jsonPointer). So node.at("/a/b") returns value 1. Expect JsonNode with int 1.

2. ref with schema id prefix: Suppose root.getId() returns "http://example.com/root". ref = "http://example.com/root#/a/b". Since schema.getId()!=null and ref starts with id, refValue = ref.substring(id.length()) => "#/a/b". Then jsonPointer = "#/a/b". Then starts with "#/", substring 1 => "/a/b". Works same.

3. ref with encoded characters: e.g., ref = "#/a%2Fb" where a/b is a key with slash. JSON: {"a/b": 2}. node.at("/a%2Fb") after URLDecoder.decode becomes "/a/b". Should get 2.

4. Missing node: ref = "#/missing". node.at returns MissingNode, then handleNullNode called. We can stub handleNullNode via spy? It's private. But we can stub root's behavior: when root.getSchemaNode().at("/missing") returns MissingNode, then handleNullNode will be called on the original schemaUnderTest (the spy). Since handleNullNode is private, we cannot stub. But we can test that method returns whatever handleNullNode returns; we can stub schemaUnderTest's private method via spy? Not possible. Instead we can test that when node missing, the method returns the result of handleNullNode; we can make schemaUnderTest a spy (real object) and override handleNullNode via a subclass (using Mockito's spy with CALLS_REAL_METHODS and then use doReturn(...).when(schemaUnderTest).handleNullNode(anyString(), any(JsonSchema.class)); However handleNullNode is private, cannot be accessed. So we cannot stub private method. So maybe we skip missing node test.

Thus implement two test methods.

Need imports: com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper, com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode, java.net.URLDecoder, etc.

Write test class with @Test methods.

Implementation details:

ObjectMapper mapper = new ObjectMapper(); JsonNode rootNode = mapper.readTree("{\"a\":{\"b\":1},\"a/b\":2}");

Now test.

Make sure to annotate with @Test.
